channel.title: Religion News Service - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Religion News Service (religionnews.com)

item.title: Ramadan’s first Friday prayers are held at Jerusalem’s Al-Aqsa Mosque
item.description: Aqsa took place for the first time since a shaky ceasefire deal between Israel and Hamas went into effect in October.

item.title: Court clears way for Louisiana law requiring Ten Commandments in classrooms to take effect
item.description: The 5th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals voted 12-6 to lift a block that a lower court first placed on the law in 2024. In the opinion released Friday, the court said it was too early to make a judgment call on the constitutionality of the law.

item.title: The bones of St. Francis are going on public display, a mixed blessing for Assisi
item.description: Already, nearly 400,000 people have registered to pray before the relics and Stoppini estimates the number could well reach a half-million before the bones go back into their tomb March 22.

item.title: Prayer app Hallow faces backlash over Lenten partnership with Tucker Carlson
item.description: Some Christian users said they planned to stop using Hallow because of its partnership with Carlson, while others praised the collaboration. Multiple users called for boycotts of the app and other sponsors.

item.title: Notre Dame professor’s appointment pits academic freedom against bishops’ authority
item.description: Who ultimately defines the boundaries of acceptable academic discourse within a Catholic institution?

item.title: Don’t misinterpret Bono’s criticism of Israel’s policies
item.description: Bono speaks as a friend of Judaism and the Jewish people. Let's give him the respect he deserves.

item.title: Before we stand on empathy, let’s decide what we mean by it
item.description: Most Americans believe empathy is foundational to a healthy society. But are we willing to do the hard work empathy requires?

item.title: Minnesota faith groups sue DHS over access to immigrant detainees
item.description: It's at least the second lawsuit challenging the federal government's policy of barring faith leaders from accessing some DHS facilities.

item.title: From Diwali parties to daily puja: Hindu campus houses push for deeper faith practice
item.description: The Vivekananda House, a Hindu student center across eight U.S. college campuses, is contributing, says students, to 'a major push in how Hindus are represented on campus.'

item.title: What’s Next for American Jews and Israel? A Half-Century of Consensus Weakens.
item.description: For 50 years, support for Israel was a central pillar of American Jewish life. That consensus is cracking. Religion reporter Yonat Shimron helps us trace how we got here — and what Oct. 7 changed.
